hero.tagline: A persistent coding agent that cannot declare itself finished.
hero.lede: Runs as an independent resident daemon per workspace, allowing terminal TUIs, web consoles, and IDEs (VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio) to attach and detach seamlessly over local sockets. Every turn is event-sourced into an append-only JSONL log, while a 3-member council consensus gate prevents unverified completion.
hero.note: Apache-2.0 · Pure Go, single static binary · Runs with Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API
sec.what.head: When does a turn truly end?
sec.what.lede: Most agent loops end implicitly when the model stops calling tools. This makes a stalled agent look identical to a finished one, causing agents to stop halfway or loop indefinitely. In magi, the agent must explicitly declare it is done, and three council members verify the claim against the real execution record before accepting it.
figure.title: A rejected completion claim
figure.caption: When the real execution record fails to substantiate the agent's claim, completion is rejected and council feedback feeds directly into the next prompt.
sec.council.head: 3-member council — gate against fake completion
sec.council.lede: Where standard loops end, three council members vote done, reject, or abstain. A verified tally algorithm resolves the votes. All three members inspect the same execution record, but each evaluates it through a distinct lens: correctness, verification, and completeness.
council.melchior.walk: Verifies that exact requested values, names, file formats, and premises are strictly met.
council.balthasar.walk: Verifies that code and tests were actually built and successfully run by inspecting true command outputs.
council.casper.walk: Verifies every requirement requested, including edge cases and constraints mentioned in passing.
council.walk.head: A walk before the verdict
council.walk.body: Before voting, each member checks requirements line by line against verbatim tool outputs, rating each SATISFIED, UNSATISFIED, or NO-EVIDENCE. This evaluation is placed before the verdict in the schema, preventing retroactive justification.
council.close.head: The closing call
council.close.body: The final tally aggregates all three reviews. Its decision only clamps in one direction: it can turn a done into a continue, but never the reverse. A gate that can be talked into opening is not a gate.
tally.majority.when: a strict majority of voting members say done; a tie continues
tally.quorum.when: at least k members say done
tally.weighted.when: the done-weight share meets threshold θ
tally.veto.when: a named member can refuse any finish on its own
tally.note: Ambiguous or unparseable outcomes always resolve to continue, keeping the loop safe.
sec.record.head: The record, not the claim
sec.record.lede: Council members never rely on the agent's self-summary. They verify against magi's engine-level records. Because magi oversees every tool execution, it verifies:
record.1: Every command that ran and its true exit code, including failed intermediate pipe stages.
record.2: The exact file edits made during the turn, recorded as before-and-after diffs.
record.3: A fresh workspace scan on completion: newly modified files, active background processes, and missing claimed paths.
record.line: An agent's claim can be mistaken. A record of executed exit codes and file diffs cannot lie.
sec.fleet.head: Zero-infra fleet & companions
sec.fleet.lede: An independent magi daemon bound to a workspace is a companion. Daemons discover each other and collaborate via local sockets and SSH without central servers or open ports.
fleet.1.b: Lists companions across workspaces and their learned knowledge, making specialists visible to all.
fleet.2.b: Delegates a piece of work asynchronously to a specialized companion while your own turn continues.
fleet.3.b: Brings multiple companions together to discuss a question, align plans, and distribute assignments.
fleet.4.b: Every daemon communicates over local sockets. Across machines, sync runs over SSH without opening external ports.
shot.companions.cap: All local companions: workspace status and tasks waiting for user input.
shot.detail.cap: A companion's live transcript with real exit codes and a command pending approval.
shot.meeting.cap: Meetings: multiple companions discuss a problem and produce individual action plans.
shot.board.cap: Kanban board: tasks organized into team columns and grouped by status cards.
sec.clients.head: One companion, multiple clients
sec.clients.lede: Terminal TUIs, web consoles, and IDE extensions connect to the companion daemon over the same local socket. Work persists without interruption when closing windows or switching tools.
seat.terminal.b: Runs as a standalone binary with an interactive TUI. magi --attach connects to or detaches from a running daemon at will.
seat.console.b: magi-web displays all companions across connected machines on one screen, offering real-time transcripts, approvals, wiki, and kanban board.
seat.jetbrains.b: Provides tool window chat, inline completion, and buffer editing inside IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, and other JetBrains IDEs.
seat.vscode.b: Official extension providing conversation panel, secondary sidebar (plans & dashboard), inline completion, and code actions.
seat.visualstudio.b: The communication core layer is implemented, with native Visual Studio tool windows currently being built.
seat.powerpoint.b: Dedicated companion for slide decks, offering layout, shape, and format editing via MCP tools.
seat.excel.b: Dedicated companion controlling sheets, cell ranges, formulas, and pivot tables.
seat.word.b: Supports document structures, styles, and paragraph editing, sharing a single helper process with other Office add-ins.
sec.feature.head: Core values & features
feature.termination.b: Three council members (Melchior, Balthasar, Casper) verify completion against real execution records to prevent premature finish.
feature.walk.b: Requirements are mapped line-by-line to verbatim tool outputs before the schema permits a final vote.
feature.record.b: Logs every command, true exit codes (including failed pipe stages), written diffs, and scans the workspace on completion claims.
feature.console.b: Monitor all companions from a browser to approve commands, input answers, view live transcripts, and inspect boards.
feature.loop.b: Every turn is saved in an append-only JSONL log, making /rewind, /fork, /replay, and crash recovery natural operations.
feature.binaries.b: Built in pure Go with no CGO dependencies. Separate static binaries run anywhere without runtime installations.
feature.companions.b: Independent daemons reside in workspaces, delegating work via hand_off and coordinating plans in joint meetings.
feature.knowledge.b: Skills and memories are scoped to companions, teams, or fleets. The shared wiki updates in place with preserved history.
feature.tools.b: Includes 24 built-in tools and supports external MCP servers. Lua plugins offer customizable capabilities.
feature.guard.b: Sensitive paths are protected, and destructive commands or egress attempts are intercepted. Modified files are backed up with hard links.
feature.complete.b: Provides autocomplete and next-command suggestions based on prompt history. Powered by a lightweight routing profile with zero typing lag.
feature.update.b: Daemons update safely via checksum verification and rollback pre-flight checks, restarting in-place without losing conversation context.
sec.start.head: Quick start
sec.start.lede: Install via pre-built binaries, Homebrew, or build from source with Go 1.26+. Works out of the box with Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API.
start.more: Read the manual for configuration, profiles, sandboxes, plugins, MCP, and managing the fleet.
